title: Harden Android WebView deep links and media permissions
body:
## Why CodeRabbit flagged issues on the merged Android wrapper. This follow-up applies the still-valid ones. ## Changes - Grant camera/microphone only for HTTPS `cursor.com` on the default port (443) - Grant only `RESOURCE_VIDEO_CAPTURE` and `RESOURCE_AUDIO_CAPTURE` - Deny a second capture request while one is pending, including already-granted Android permissions - Accept incoming deep links only as `https://cursor.com/agents…` without `.` / `..` segments, non-default ports, or backslash traversal - Parse `intent:` URLs with `Intent.parseUri` and clear package/component/selector - Reload home when `WebView.restoreState` returns no history - CI: `permissions: contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false` - Unit tests for origins, ports, and deep-link path traversal Local `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` passed.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Security** - Restricted deep links to HTTPS `cursor.com` and `www.cursor.com` `/agents` destinations. - Rejected non-default ports and unsafe dot-segment paths. - Limited media access requests to supported camera and microphone permissions. - Allowed trusted HTTPS media origins only from approved Cursor domains. - Sanitized external intent URLs before launching them. - **Navigation** - Preserved approved authentication destinations, including Google Accounts and Cursor authentication hosts. - **Testing** - Added automated coverage for deep-link, authentication, media-origin, and domain validation. - Expanded Android build validation to include unit tests.
